A single continuous locked-off tripod shot of a traditional Indian village temple courtyard, illustrated as a 1950s Indian devotional book painting in matte opaque gouache and egg tempera.
The camera is completely fixed in position and orientation for the entire shot. The framing remains identical from beginning to end. The distance between the camera and every stationary object remains constant. The temple, banyan tree, courtyard paving and surrounding village buildings remain in exactly the same screen positions and at the same apparent size.
A calm Indian spiritual figure with dark wavy hair, wearing an off-white cotton dhoti and shawl, stands peacefully in the courtyard. He makes one extremely small, natural head movement and gently breathes. A few leaves move subtly in the breeze.
Only these small movements occur. The background remains stationary. The figure stays in the same position and at the same apparent size throughout the shot.
A completely static wide composition, with no camera movement, no push-in, no zoom, no dolly, no pan, no tilt, no reframing and no cuts. Preserve the supplied painting's character, architecture, colors, lighting, soft sepia contours and hand-painted gouache texture from the first frame through the final frame.
